$comment: The group's default packing list. This file is the starting point, not the
current state: anything anyone adds, edits or removes on the Packing page is
an operation appended to the shared log, and the page shows this file with
Because a removal is an operation rather than a deletion, an item left here
can always be restored. Edit this file to change what a brand-new device
starts from; edit on the site to change what the group sees.
category  : must match an id in `categories` below
essential : reserved for what cannot be bought on the way and would change
the trip if forgotten. Kept deliberately short — Chamonix and
Courmayeur both have shops, so most of this list is recoverable
and marking it all essential would make the filter useless.
note      : why it is on the list, or what is specific to this trip. Left
empty where the item speaks for itself.
What is NOT here: whether *you* have packed something. That is per-person
and stays on your own device, because six people ticking off the same

items.name: Broken-in hiking boots
items.note: Broken in over months, not weeks. Seven consecutive days with cols in them is not the place to discover a pressure point.

items.name: Hiking socks (4 pairs)
items.note: Two in rotation, two drying. Wool, not cotton.

items.name: Liner socks
items.note: Worth it if you are blister-prone.

items.name: Base layer tops (2)
items.note: Merino or synthetic. One on, one drying.

items.name: Sun hat or cap
items.note: Long exposed traverses above the treeline with no shade.

items.name: Sunglasses
items.note: Category 3 or better. Glare off the snow patches on the higher cols is fierce enough to matter over a full day.

items.name: Trekking poles
items.note: The descents are what wreck knees on this route, not the climbs.

items.name: Insulated jacket
items.note: Cols sit above 2,500 m and mornings are cold regardless of the July date.

items.name: Waterproof jacket
items.note: Properly waterproof with a hood, not a windbreaker. Afternoon storms build fast in the valleys.

items.name: Light gloves
items.note: For the early starts on col mornings.

items.name: Evening clothes
items.note: One set to change into. Everything else is hiking kit.

items.name: Daypack (30-35 L)
items.note: Sized for a day, not the whole trip — the shared bags go by transfer.

items.name: Pack rain cover or liner
items.note: A bin liner inside the pack is more reliable than a cover in wind.

items.name: Dry bags or zip bags
items.note: Keeping the down jacket and the electronics dry matters more than keeping everything dry.

items.name: Duffel for the luggage transfer
items.note: Two big bags are shared across the group rather than one each — see the luggage line on the Money page.

items.name: Sleeping bag liner
items.note: Required at Auberge de la Nova and the Trient gîte. Refuges provide blankets and a pillow but not sheets, and a liner is usually mandatory rather than optional.

items.name: Earplugs
items.note: Dormitory nights. Not negotiable if you want to sleep before a col morning.

items.name: Sandals or hut shoes
items.note: Boots come off at the door in every refuge, and it is worth having your feet out of them anyway.

items.name: Quick-dry towel
items.note: Refuges rarely provide one; the hotels will.

items.name: Toiletries
items.note: Small. Anything you can buy in Courmayeur on the rest day does not need carrying from home.

items.name: Blister kit
items.note: Hydrocolloid dressings and tape. The single most likely thing to end someone's walking.

items.name: First aid basics
items.note: Painkillers, antihistamine, plasters, tweezers. One decent kit shared across the group is enough.

items.name: Sunscreen (SPF 50)
items.note: Altitude plus snow reflection. Reapply at the cols.

items.name: Personal medication
items.note: Enough for the whole trip plus a few days. Pharmacies exist in Chamonix and Courmayeur and nowhere else on the route.

items.name: Passport
items.note: The route crosses into Italy and Switzerland on foot. Nobody checks, but carry it.

items.name: Travel and rescue insurance
items.note: Check that mountain rescue is covered. Switzerland is not in the EU health scheme.

items.name: Cash in euros
items.note: Les Chapieux is card-unreliable and the navette machine wants coins. Budget more than feels necessary.

items.name: Cash in Swiss francs
items.note: For La Fouly, Champex and Trient. Small Swiss places often refuse euros or use a poor rate.

items.name: Bank card with no foreign fees
Booking confirmations
items.note: Saved offline, not just sitting in email. Assume no signal when you arrive.

items.name: Power bank
items.note: Refuge sockets are scarce and shared between everyone in the dormitory.

items.name: Plug adapters (EU and Swiss)
items.note: Switzerland uses a different socket from France and Italy, and a standard EU plug does not always fit it.

items.name: Head torch
items.note: For pre-dawn starts, and for finding the dormitory bathroom without waking the room.

items.name: Offline maps downloaded
items.note: This site caches its own tiles from the About page. Do it on hotel wifi, not on the trail.

items.name: Camera
items.note: The Days pages list the light plan for each scenery stop.

items.name: Water bottles or bladder (2 L)
items.note: Two litres of capacity. Refill at refuges and village fountains rather than carrying a full day's worth.

items.name: Trail snacks
items.note: Half board covers dinner and breakfast at most stops, so lunch and snacks are the gap.

items.name: Small knife
items.note: Checked baggage only.

items.name: Travel wash and a line
items.note: The Courmayeur rest day is the one realistic laundry stop.

items.name: Sit pad
items.note: Lunch stops are on wet rock more often than not.

items.name: Book or cards
items.note: Refuge evenings are long and there is no signal.
